lede.headline: Samsung's profit nearly nine-folds on the AI memory boom
lede.dek: Samsung Electronics guided to a record operating profit for the third quarter on AI-fueled memory-chip demand, on a day that also brought a mixed bag of bank and luxury earnings and a stark warning from Broadcom's CEO about AI financing.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: JPMorgan profit rises but securities losses sting
stories.move: JPMorgan Chase's third-quarter net income rose 6% to $15.3 billion and revenue climbed 8% to $50.2 billion, according to the bank's own SEC filing. Diluted earnings per share were $5.57, up from $5.07 a year earlier. The bank booked $658 million in investment-securities losses during the quarter, and investment banking fees rose 13% from a year ago but fell 8% from the second quarter.
stories.why: JPMorgan's results are a bellwether for corporate borrowing and trading activity, so a securities loss and softer sequential investment-banking fees raise questions about how long the current trading boom can keep accelerating.
stories.bear: Net income, revenue and per-share earnings all rose from a year ago, and investment banking fees are still up double digits year over year, so the quarter looks solid by its own numbers.
stories.watch: JPMorgan's updated outlook for about $107 billion in 2027 net interest income excluding markets.

stories.headline: Citigroup profit jumps 40% but shares still slide
stories.move: Citigroup's third-quarter net income rose 40% to $5.2 billion, or $2.85 a share, beating the roughly $2.62 analyst estimate, on revenue up 8% to $23.85 billion, the bank's earnings release showed. CEO Jane Fraser said the bank is "continuing to invest in growth" while preparing for an AI-driven future. Shares still fell about 5.6% that day.
stories.why: A profit beat that still gets sold off signals investors are more focused on the pace of trading and credit costs ahead than on the quarter that just closed.
stories.bear: A 40% profit jump and 15% growth in wealth management are hard to call bad news; some of the drop may reflect bank stocks giving back gains built up ahead of earnings.
stories.watch: Whether Citigroup can keep beating its own 11-13% near-term return target next quarter.

stories.headline: LVMH's China slump drags on fashion division
stories.move: LVMH's revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached 57.1 billion euros, up 2% organically but down 2% on a reported basis, the company's own release showed. Third-quarter organic growth slowed to 1% from 3% in the prior quarter. Fashion & Leather Goods, LVMH's largest division and home to Louis Vuitton and Dior, posted a 5% organic sales drop in the quarter to 8.25 billion euros, which the company attributed to slowing demand in China. Shares fell about 1.7% on Oct. 13, the day after the report.
stories.why: Fashion & Leather Goods is LVMH's main profit engine, so a second straight quarter of China-driven weakness there raises doubts about how soon the luxury slowdown turns around.
stories.bear: The U.S., Europe and Japan all grew well in the quarter, and LVMH says it remains confident in its full-year outlook despite what it calls an uncertain environment.
stories.watch: LVMH's full-year 2026 results, due early 2027, for whether China demand stabilizes.

stories.headline: Broadcom CEO says capital, not chips, now limits AI
stories.move: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said at a conference in Singapore on Oct. 12 that access to capital, not chip or memory supply, is becoming the main constraint on AI buildouts. He said some AI investors "have no clue what they are investing in" and are setting expectations so extreme that it is "almost like they are in a casino," 247wallst.com reported. Broadcom shares fell 1.88% to close at $354.73 the next trading day.
stories.why: Tan runs one of the AI boom's biggest chip suppliers, so a warning from him about how AI infrastructure is being financed carries more weight than the usual outside skeptic's take.
stories.bear: Tan also said compute demand looks likely to stay strong through 2030 and that chip and memory shortages are easing, which is a bullish read on the underlying business even as he's wary of its financing.
stories.watch: Broadcom's next quarterly report for whether AI infrastructure orders are still growing.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms nears India's biggest-ever IPO
stories.move: Reliance's Jio Platforms filed its draft IPO prospectus with India's securities regulator SEBI on June 19, 2026 and received SEBI's approval on Aug. 28. The offering is reported at about 37,700 crore rupees (roughly $4 billion), entirely new shares, with proceeds going mainly to repay Jio debt, Angel One reported. Roadshows wrapped up in September and October, led by Akash Ambani, who called the listing "a great responsibility" and the Reliance group's first public share sale in nearly three decades, alongside his sister Isha Ambani.
stories.why: A Jio listing of this size would be India's largest IPO on record and a major test of investor appetite for its telecom-and-digital business separate from parent Reliance Industries.
stories.bear: The exact subscription dates, price band and listing date are still not formally confirmed by Jio or the exchanges, so the terms could still shift before launch.
stories.watch: Jio's expected subscription window around Oct. 21-23 and a listing near Oct. 28.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery's IPO window closes after profit surge
stories.move: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery's "people's IPO" subscription window ran from Sept. 14 to Oct. 13, offering about 4.1 billion ordinary shares at 525 naira each, AllAfrica reported. The refinery posted first-half 2026 after-tax profit of roughly $1.82 billion, reversing a $476 million loss for all of 2025, as average plant utilization rose to 83.6% from about 45% at the start of the year.
stories.why: A successful listing would make Aliko Dangote's refinery a public company for the first time, after years of construction delays and losses.
stories.bear: Allotment and listing aren't finalized yet, and some of the company's own revenue and fundraising figures didn't fully reconcile in reporting, so the final outcome of the offer is still unclear.
stories.watch: The refinery's planned listing, expected in late November.

stories.headline: HCLTech profit rises 21% on record deal bookings
stories.move: HCLTech reported fiscal second-quarter net profit of 5,132 crore rupees, up 21% year over year, on revenue of 35,620 crore rupees, up 11.5%, for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, the company said. New deal bookings rose 27% to about $3.26 billion, a first-half record, and the board declared a 12-rupee-a-share interim dividend. Shares rallied the next trading day.
stories.why: Strong bookings suggest enterprise clients are still signing new IT and AI-services contracts even as some peers describe a more cautious spending environment.
stories.bear: HCL's software unit revenue fell 11.2% in constant currency, and the company left its full-year revenue growth guidance unchanged at a modest 2.5%-4%, so the quarter wasn't a breakout across the whole business.
stories.watch: Whether this quarter's record bookings convert into faster revenue growth later in the fiscal year.

stories.headline: Samsung guides to record profit on AI memory demand
stories.move: Samsung Electronics guided on Oct. 8 to third-quarter consolidated operating profit of about 107.4 trillion won, nearly nine times the 12.2 trillion won it posted a year earlier, on sales of about 195 trillion won, Hargreaves Lansdown reported. The preliminary, company-estimated figures are required under Korean disclosure rules and don't break results out by division; the detailed report with segment figures is due later this month.
stories.why: The jump points to how much revenue memory-chip makers are now pulling in from AI data-center demand for high-bandwidth and other advanced memory.
stories.bear: The guidance is preliminary with no division breakdown yet, and the reported sales figure actually came in below analysts' consensus forecast.
stories.watch: Samsung's detailed Q3 report, expected later this month, for the semiconductor division's actual contribution.

quickHits: Tesla delivered more than 486,000 vehicles in the third quarter, topping the company-compiled consensus, ahead of its Oct. 21 earnings call.
memo: Even strong earnings can mean a falling stock price when expectations run ahead of results — manage what the market expects, not just the numbers themselves.
A warning from the CEO of a major AI chip supplier that "capital, not chips" is now the constraint is a sign the financing terms behind AI infrastructure deals are worth watching closely.
China-dependent demand is still weighing on luxury and conglomerate earnings; plans that assume a quick China recovery look riskier right now.

movers.why: Citigroup fell 5.6% after third-quarter profit beat estimates but trading trends and credit costs worried investors, Beinsure reported.
